prompt:
A single compound was assayed by IC50 against a single protein target in two different assays, reported in the literature.

Compound SMILES: O=c1[nH]c(CCCN2CC=C(c3ccc(F)cc3)CC2)nc2ccccc12
Target (ChEMBL): CHEMBL3105

Assay A:
  Description: In vitro inhibitory concentration against human recombinant Poly (ADP-ribose) polymerase 1
  Assay type: B
  ChEMBL confidence score: 9
  Organism: Homo sapiens

Assay B:
  Description: Inhibition of human PARP1
  Assay type: B
  ChEMBL confidence score: 9
  Organism: Homo sapiens

Will the two reported IC50 values agree closely (within 0.3 log units), or differ substantially (more than 1.0 log units)?

Respond with exactly this JSON and nothing else:
{"call": "COMMENSURABLE" | "NOT_COMMENSURABLE" | "INSUFFICIENT_INFO",
 "confidence": <float 0-1>,
 "error_class": "assay_method" | "buffer_conditions" | "construct_mutant" | "organism" | "readout_type" | "potency_range" | "none" | "other",
 "reason": "<one sentence>"}

"COMMENSURABLE" means you expect the two reported values to agree closely.
"NOT_COMMENSURABLE" means you expect them to differ substantially.
error_class is your primary reason for a NOT_COMMENSURABLE call, else "none".
raw:
```json
{
  "call": "INSUFFICIENT_INFO",
  "confidence": 0.9,
  "error_class": "assay_method",
  "reason": "The lack of details regarding the substrate (NAD+) concentration and specific detection methodology prevents determining commensurability, as PARP1 IC50 values are highly dependent on these experimental conditions."
}
```

parsed.reason: The lack of details regarding the substrate (NAD+) concentration and specific detection methodology prevents determining commensurability, as PARP1 IC50 values are highly dependent on these experimental conditions.
